}

pub fn load_config_file(path: &Path) -> Result<BivvyConfig> {
    let content = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| {
        if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound {
            BivvyError::ConfigNotFound { path: path.to_path_buf() }
        } else {
            BivvyError::Io(e)
        }
    })?;
    parse_config(&content, path)
}

pub fn parse_config(content: &str, source_path: &Path) -> Result<BivvyConfig> {
    serde_yaml::from_str(content).map_err(|e| BivvyError::ConfigParseError {
        path: source_path.to_path_buf(),
        message: e.to_string(),
    })
}
```

pub fn validate(config: &BivvyConfig) -> Result<()> {
    let errors = validate_config(config);
    if errors.is_empty() {

    } else {
        let messages: Vec<_> = errors.iter().map(|e| e.message.clone()).collect();
        Err(BivvyError::ConfigValidationError {
            message: messages.join("; "),
        })
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum BivvyError {
    // Configuration errors (3 variants)
    #[error("Configuration not found: {path}")]
    ConfigNotFound { path: PathBuf },
    
    #[error("Failed to parse config at {path}: {message}")]
    ConfigParseError { path: PathBuf, message: String },
    
    #[error("Invalid configuration: {message}")]
    ConfigValidationError { message: String },
    
    // Template/Dependency errors (2 variants)
    #[error("Unknown template: {name}")]
    UnknownTemplate { name: String },
    
    #[error("Circular dependency detected: {cycle}")]
    CircularDependency { cycle: String },
    
    // Execution errors (4 variants)
    #[error("Step '{step}' failed: {message}")]
    StepExecutionError { step: String, message: String },
    
    #[error("Command failed with exit code {code:?}: {command}")]
    CommandFailed { command: String, code: Option<i32> },
    
    #[error("Missing requirement '{requirement}': {message}")]
    RequirementMissing { requirement: String, message: String },
    
    #[error("Requirement check failed for '{requirement}': {message}")]
    RequirementCheckFailed { requirement: String, message: String },
    
    // Shell errors (1 variant)
    #[error("Shell error: {message}")]
    ShellError { message: String },
    
    // IO errors (1 variant with #[from])
    #[error("IO error: {0}")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
    
    // Catch-all (1 variant with #[from])
    #[error(transparent)]
    Other(#[from] anyhow::Error),
}

// Result type alias
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, BivvyError>;

### 9. KEY CHARACTERISTICS

**Error Handling Design Strengths**:
1. ✅ Clear separation: domain errors (BivvyError) vs unexpected (anyhow)
2. ✅ Comprehensive error variants with rich context (paths, messages, step names)

**Error Handling Trade-offs**:
- **anyhow in internal modules** (cache, state, updates): Simpler but less structured; OK for internal operations
- **BivvyError in public/CLI-facing code**: Rich structure; required for proper user interaction
- **No custom Result wrapper** for anyhow modules: They bubble errors up to BivvyError catch-all

**Module Cohesion**:
- Clear error boundaries: Each module defines what errors it can produce
- Error aggregation happens at CLI command level (pattern matching)
- Root cause always preserved (no error swallowing via `.ok()`)
